reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset, and Brown distinguish being tempted toward evil, which God cannot experience, from being tested or tried, the sense in which Jesus's wilderness ordeal falls.

discrepancy.note: Strauss argues the wilderness temptation cannot really match Hebrews's claim that Jesus was tried in all things as we are, since a literal devil made his trial unlike ours.

quotes.text: and, according to Heb. iv. 15, tempted in all things like as we are; for the fullest measure of trial fell to his share in after life, and a temptation, effected by the devil in person, would rather make him unlike us, who are spared such appearances.
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined (1846), ch. on the temptation, on John 1:1 and James 1:13.

sides.snippet: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
sides.verseText: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

sides.snippet: Let no man say when he is tempted, \"I am tempted by God,\" for God can't be tempted by evil, and he himself tempts no one.
sides.verseText: Let no man say when he is tempted, \"I am tempted by God,\" for God can't be tempted by evil, and he himself tempts no one.
